message.content:
This is a read-only research task in the Zimmermann PWA Kit repo (a Salesforce Commerce Cloud PWA Kit override project) at /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa. Do NOT modify any files — this is investigation only.

CONTEXT: I'm assessing Jira ticket SFCC-201 "Product Catalogue Config – Category Merchandising Rules," which is a Business-Manager-configuration-only story (manual product pinning + rules-based ordering for category pages, all out-of-the-box SFCC functionality, explicitly "no PWA build associated with this story"). I want to verify from the actual PWA codebase whether the PLP/category product-listing code path passes through SFCC's default category sort order untouched, or whether it hardcodes/overrides a sort parameter in a way that would fight or ignore whatever a Business Manager merchandising rule configures.

WHAT TO DO:
1. Find where the PLP (product-listing/category page) fetches its product list — likely under overrides/app/pages/ (search for a category/product-list page) or a related hook. Look for usage of the SFCC Shopper Product Search / Search API (commerce-sdk-react hooks like useProductSearch, useSearchProducts, or similar) in that page's data-fetching code.
2. Check specifically: does the code pass an explicit `sort` / `sortingRule` / `refine` query parameter by default when no shopper-selected sort is active? Or does it omit the sort param so SFCC applies the category's own configured default sorting rule automatically? Quote the relevant lines and their file path + line numbers.
3. Also check overrides/app/pages/ for a category or product-list page component name (it may be under a name like product-list, category, or similar — search broadly, don't assume an exact name).
4. Report: (a) the exact file path(s) and line numbers of the relevant data-fetching code, (b) whether a default sort value is hardcoded anywhere that could override BM's merchandising rule, (c) whether there's any TODO/comment referencing merchandising rules, category sort, or SFCC-201 anywhere in the codebase (grep for "merchandis" case-insensitive across the repo, excluding node_modules), (d) whether this page is even implemented yet at all, or still a stub/placeholder from the base SFCC template (i.e., has Zimmermann actually overridden it, or is it untouched upstream code).

Keep your report under 300 words, factual, with file:line citations. This is purely descriptive fact-finding to support a backlog-refinement sizing note — no code changes, no opinions on whether anything should change.

/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.docs/temp/openItems.md:53:2. **SFCC vs Contentful content ownership on composed pages.** The principle is settled — SFCC is the source of truth for all commerce data (product attributes, pricing, inventory, variations, gallery, category and search results) and Contentful owns standalone editorial (homepage, campaign landing pages, banners, lookbooks, size guides, footer). 8	import {useLocation} from 'react-router-dom'
9	import queryString from 'query-string'
10	
11	// Constants
12	import {DEFAULT_SEARCH_PARAMS} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/constants'
13	
14	const PARSE_OPTIONS = {
15	    parseBooleans: true,
16	    parseNumbers: true
17	}
18	
19	/*
20	 * This hook will return all the location search params pertinant
21	 * to the product list page.
22	 */
23	export const useSearchParams = (searchParams = DEFAULT_SEARCH_PARAMS, parseRefine = true) => {
24	    const {search} = useLocation()
25	
26	    // Encode the search query, including preset values.
27	    const searchParamsObject = {
28	        ...searchParams,
29	        ...parse(search.substring(1), parseRefine)
30	    }
31	
32	    return [searchParamsObject, {stringify, parse}]
33	}
34	
35	/**
36	 * Encode's the provided search parameters object, paying special attention to ensure
37	 * that the child `refine` object is alway encoded correctly.
38	 *
39	 * @param {Object} searchParamsObj
40	 * @returns
41	 */
42	export const stringify = (searchParamsObj) => {
43	    let searchParamsObjCopy = {...searchParamsObj}
44	
45	    // Remove our copy of the original refinement value so it's not stringified.
46	    delete searchParamsObjCopy._refine
47	
48	    // "stringify" the nested refinements
49	    searchParamsObjCopy.refine = Object.keys(searchParamsObjCopy.refine).map((key) =>
50	        queryString.stringify(
51	            {[key]: searchParamsObjCopy.refine[key]},
52	            {
53	                arrayFormat: 'separator',
54	                arrayFormatSeparator: '|',
55	                encode: false
56	            }
57	        )
58	    )
59	
60	    // "stringify" the entire object
61	    searchParamsObjCopy = queryString.stringify(searchParamsObjCopy)
62	    return searchParamsObjCopy
63	}
64	
65	/**
66	 * Decode's the provided query string representation of a search parameter object, paying
67	 * special attention to also decode the 'refine' object.
68	 *
69	 * @param {Object} searchParamsStr
70	 * @param {Boolean} parseRefine - opt out of parsing the inner refine object.
71	 * @returns
72	 */
73	export const parse = (searchParamsStr, parseRefine = true) => {
74	    const params = queryString.parse(searchParamsStr, PARSE_OPTIONS)
75	
76	    // Ensure the refinments is an array (make it easier to manipulate).
77	    params.refine = Array.isArray(params.refine) ? params.refine : [params.refine].filter(Boolean)
78	
79	    // Parse the nested refinement entries.
80	    if (parseRefine) {
81	        params._refine = params.refine
82	        params.refine = params.refine.reduce((acc, curr) => {
83	            return {
84	                ...acc,
85	                ...queryString.parse(curr, {
86	                    ...PARSE_OPTIONS,
87	                    parseNumbers: false,
88	                    arrayFormat: 'separator',
89	                    arrayFormatSeparator: '|'
90	                })
91	            }
92	        }, {})
93	    }
94	
95	    return params
96	}

## Findings: SFCC-201 PLP Sort-Order Code Path

**(d) Is the page overridden?** No. `overrides/app/pages/` contains only `product-detail`, `home`, `experience`, `contentfulPreview`, `my-new-route` — no `product-list`/`category` directory exists. In `overrides/app/routes.tsx:51`, the route array does `..._routes` (spreading `routes` imported from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/routes` at line 15) with no preceding override entry for `/category/:categoryId` or `/search` (contrast with the explicit PDP override callout in the comment at lines 26-32). So the PLP/category page is **100% untouched upstream SFCC PWA Kit template code** at `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/product-list/index.jsx`.

**(a)/(b) Data-fetching and sort handling** (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/product-list/index.jsx`):
- Line 129: `const [searchParams, ...] = useSearchParams()`
- Lines 142-143: injects `cgid=${params.categoryId}` into `_refine`
- Lines 156-158: strips `_refine`, builds `refine` array
- Lines 160-186: calls `useProductSearch({parameters: {...restOfParams, ..., refine}})` — `restOfParams` (spread from `searchParams`) carries whatever `sort` value is present.

The default comes from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/constants.js:18`: `DEFAULT_SEARCH_PARAMS = {limit: 25, offset: 0, sort: 'best-matches', refine: []}`, merged with URL params in `use-search-params.js:23-30`. So **every category/search request always sends an explicit `sort` param** — `best-matches` unless the shopper picks a different option — it is never omitted. Neither `overrides/app/hooks` nor `overrides/app/constants/index.ts` redefines `use-search-params.js` or `DEFAULT_SEARCH_PARAMS`/sort. Whether SFCC's Search API resolves `sort=best-matches` to the category's BM-assigned default sorting rule is platform behavior outside this repo's code.

**(c) Merchandising references:** `grep -rni "merchandis"` (excl. node_modules/.git) hits only `.docs/prd/plp.md:79-80` (SPR-18), `.docs/prd/search.md`, `.docs/prd/pricing-currency-globale.md`, `.docs/prd/cart.md` — all PRD/planning markdown, zero hits in `overrides/app/**` code. No SFCC-201 references anywhere.
